name: Oakley Han
life: “I still remember a waiter ironing my sleeves before our first opening.” On Saturday, near Harbour Bakery, Oakley buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I want it lined in cold blue like the restaurant I used to run.
appearance: Oakley has a gray streak running back from the forehead, full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, and a favorite piece of clothing, a pale blue work shirt. It usually goes with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. When somebody else has the floor, Oakley starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak.
personality: Oakley loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Oakley remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To host a Sunday dinner in the blue-lined coat.
family: Silas Voss is Oakley’s younger cousin. Oakley remembers the birthdays. Silas asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A scar at the salon*, Silas says, “I wrote a manipulative slogan about survival and took it out before the presentation.”
connections: Noel Aubin (housecoat maker). They measure a garment for a whole Sunday, including sitting at the head of the table.

reactions.situation: A visitor asks where the housecoat was bought
reactions.response: Oakley gives the maker the chance to be credited without revealing what the garment cost.
